name: – Inese Vaidere – Commission proposal
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the modification of customs duties applicable to imports of certain goods originating in or exported directly or indirectly from the Russian Federation and the Republic of Belarus
part_text:
The European Parliament backs a plan to raise import duties on fertilisers and farm goods coming from Russia and Belarus. Tariffs on nitrogen-based fertilisers would go up gradually over three years, making Russian supplies too expensive so buyers switch to other countries or European producers. The aim is to stop money flowing to Russia's war effort and to protect European food supplies. The Parliament also wants the Commission to watch fertiliser prices closely and help farmers if costs jump.

- Higher duties phase in on Russian and Belarusian fertilisers and remaining farm imports.
- Affects EU farmers, fertiliser producers and importers; prices to be monitored monthly.
- Parliament adopted its position; the regulation should apply from 1 July 2025.
